name: Structural Consequences of Peripheral Recursion
statement: Every member of $\mathcal R_{\mathrm{per}}$ is tree-like, ample, dismantlable ample, almost-median, and proper semi-median. Its maximal-cube intersection graph is dismantlable, its alternating cube count is one, and its cubical complex is collapsible and contractible. A regular member is a hypercube. The class is not closed under arbitrary induced or isometric subgraphs.
proof: The class implications follow inductively from the two-child peripheral decomposition. The enumerative and topological conclusions are inherited from ampleness and corner peeling; regular tree-like partial cubes are hypercubes. For nonclosure, $Q_3$ belongs to the class but its induced isometric middle-level six-cycle is periphery-free.
